ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line AB and line CD intersect at point O, with OM $\perp$ AB. If $\angle 1=40^\circ$ and $\angle 2= 30^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle$NOD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since OM$\perp$AB,\\
it follows that $\angle$AOM= $90^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle$1=$40^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$AOC=$\angle$AOM−$\angle$1= $90^\circ−40^\circ= 50^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle$2=$30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle$NOD=$\angle$DOC−$\angle$AOC−$\angle$2= $\boxed{100^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, straight line AB passes horizontally through point O, A is on the left side, B is on the right side; straight line CD passes obliquely through point O, C is at the upper left, D is at the lower right, therefore C, O, D are collinear. Ray OM goes upward from O, and the problem stem gives OM ⟂ AB. Ray ON points from O toward the lower left. The ∠1 marked in the figure is located between OC and OM, namely ∠COM; the marked ∠2 is located between OA and ON, namely ∠AON. Reasoning: Because OM ⟂ AB, ∠AOM = 90°. Also because ∠1 = ∠COM = 40°, ∠AOC = ∠AOM − ∠COM = 90° − 40° = 50°. Because C, O, D are on the same straight line, ∠COD = 180°. This straight angle from OC to OD is successively divided by ∠AOC, ∠AON and ∠NOD into three parts, among which ∠AON = ∠2 = 30°. Therefore ∠NOD = 180° − 50° − 30° = 100°.
